svg.text: GAUSSIAN FILTER rounds the corners so the signal doesn't splatter into neighbouring channels
THE CARRIER: a little faster for 1, a little slower for 0 (drawn hugely slowed down)
To send a bit, the radio nudges its frequency a little up (±≈160 kHz around the channel centre) for a 1 and down for a 0: frequency-shift
keying. Smoothing the switch with a Gaussian curve keeps the energy inside the 1 MHz channel. Faster “EDR” modes (2–3 Mbit/s) also shift the
wave's phase, which is how earbuds fit high-quality audio through the air.
GFSK: bits as small shifts in frequency
